answer: Committee shuffling by verifiable randomness resists sybils. Each epoch every identity is drawn into one small validation thread, and committees never persist. An attacker floods the ocean of registrations with fakes, but cannot choose where they land, so their influence stays near its nadir without winning many draws. Each fake still pays the entry bond and per-epoch duty, fees are burned, and seats are capped, so cost grows linearly with fakes while expected gains stay flat. Mass registration becomes a losing trade.
